name: Sasha Võ
aliases: the gunslinger east of the Junction
role: Independent contract operator. Ex-Sigma-program subject — a different secondary facility, a different generation of NeoCortex hardware than Kyle's, a different (and earlier) walking-out. Pistol specialist with her own intact array running its own degradation timeline. Crossed paths with Kyle during a contract overlap; the two of them got out of the same building on the same night for entirely different reasons and have not pretended since to be more to each other than that.
status: alive — at large, operating independently in the GLMZ east of the Lateral Junction and into the buffer zones
location: Currently: unknown — somewhere east of the Lateral Junction, on a contract she did not log with Sable. Will reach out when she has something to trade.
description:
Twenty-eight years old. Ex-Sigma-program subject — a different secondary corponation facility from the Atlas program that built Kyle, on a different continent's research lineage, generations apart in implant architecture. Her NeoCortex array is a Sigma-line build at 24,576 electrode density (smaller than Kyle's 32,768 Atlas, larger than the consumer Tier-3 implants the legitimate market sells), drilled-in firmware that runs cleaner than Kyle's because the Sigma program had the calibration discipline Atlas never bothered with. The trade-off is generation-specific: Sigma arrays are stable for about twelve to fifteen years before a slow ferromagnetic drift starts; she is at year ten and has begun managing the drift with a pharmaceutical regimen she compounds herself. She has approximately five years before the array degrades past field-operable. She does not talk about this.

She is not Kyle's heir, his ward, his bloodline successor, or his tissue-match continuation. The two of them are unrelated. They have different facility codes, different program lineages, different hardware generations, different scars at the back of the skull. Their faces do not echo each other. The reason they look at each other with recognition is the curriculum they both survived — the same shape of confinement, the same shape of metric-driven training, the same shape of being a unit-of-work to people who never used your name. Recognition is not lineage. They settled this within thirty seconds of meeting.

Her heritage is the Ubiquitous Diaspora at its most mixed: Vietnamese (paternal line, surname Võ — written 武 in the syllabary her grandfather kept), Ukrainian (the first name and the cool-winter undertone), and Senegalese (the geometry around the jaw and the way her hair takes the light). The face is not Kyle's. The face is hers, and she has never had to share it with a recorded predecessor.

Fully trained. Sigma's curriculum was firearms-heavy from age twelve onward — her parents volunteered her into the program at age eleven for what they understood to be a corponation educational pipeline; what it actually was, neither parent has lived long enough to learn. She walked out at twenty-one when the program shifted from training to deployment-readiness and she realized she did not want to be the asset she was about to be assigned as. She has been operating independently for seven years, building a contract pipeline through fixers in the eastern farmlands and Pulse-hub stations, no permanent residence, no permanent crew, no favorite pistol and no jacket older than the last contract.

She is expressive where Kyle is reserved. She talks through what she is doing while she is doing it, she asks strangers questions, she tests jokes to see if they land and tries another when the first one doesn't. She revels in what she is good at. The first time she shot a person who was going to stay dead from it (age twenty-two, third contract out of the program, a clean payment for an unclean target), she lingered on the grip afterward the way you linger on a thing you have known was in you all along and have just finally gotten to use.

Pistols are her specialty and her preference. The grip is different on every frame — single-action, double-action, recoil mass, trigger pull, safety geometry, magazine capacity — and Sigma drilled that variance into her specifically because the program wanted a shooter who could run anything. She does not carry a favorite. She does not name her weapon. She does not keep mementos. When the pistol in her hand runs dry she drops it and takes the next one off whoever is on the ground, and the new weapon is in her grip inside a second, calibrated inside another, firing correctly by the third.

Her counting tic (rivets, tiles, rain impacts) is still there but quieter than it used to be — seven years on the road taught her to suppress it in company. She counts under her breath only when she wants to, as self-regulation during high-cognitive moments. When she does not want to, she talks. She talks a lot. She narrates what she is seeing, what she is deciding, what she is going to try next. She plays at accents she has heard once. She calls people friend and trouble and the one with the boots, testing nicknames the way she tests jokes. She makes eye contact and holds it the way Kyle never does.

When she met Kyle — at a corponation facility on the night he was being extracted via False Death Protocol for a different contract entirely — she had been there for her own job (extraction of a Sigma-program firmware archive that the facility had been holding for a competitor's research division). They surfaced into the same hallway at the same minute with weapons in hand and recognized each other's hardware-signature within two seconds. The cooperation was tactical, brief, and clean: she pulled him out of an ambush in the maintenance corridor he had not seen coming, he opened her path to the loading bay where her contact's vehicle was waiting, neither of them owed the other anything beyond *thanks.* At dawn she walked east. Kyle walked west. They have not spoken since. She will reach out when she has something to trade.

core_fears: Becoming reserved. Becoming careful. Becoming the kind of operator who survived by not enjoying it.
The Sigma drift accelerating past her current pharmaceutical regimen — losing the array before she has built the reputation that lets her live without it
Outliving the people whose nicknames she has collected without learning what to do with the grief

That the next program — Tau, Omega, whatever the corponations call the next iteration — has already started a subject who will be better at this than she is, and will not have her seven-year head start
core_desires: To find out what she is by using herself — every job is a test, every stranger is a lesson
To make someone laugh who she did not grow up listening to
A reputation she built without anyone handing it to her — the contract pipeline is hers, the rumor is hers, the file the next operator reads is one she wrote with her own hands
Five more years of clean work before the Sigma drift forces a hard decision
coping_mechanisms: Talking — running commentary on her own actions, out loud, whether or not anyone is listening
Naming things — people, weapons, streets — before she has a reason to
Testing jokes. Watching the face for the response. Filing what worked.
Running toward the thing she is scared of, on the theory that the fear is information and information is not lethal
Counting, still, but silently and only when the social cost of counting out loud is higher than the regulation cost of suppressing it
Compounds her own pharmaceutical regimen for the array drift — the doing is part of how she manages the worry
blind_spots: She thinks being expressive is the same as being honest. It is not always.

She has not yet examined whether enjoying what she is good at is the same failure-mode the program was engineering for — she assumes enjoyment is freedom because the program tried to optimize the enjoyment out of her at thirteen and failed
She underestimates how visible the Sigma-program tells are to anyone who knows what to look for — gait economy, exit-tracking, the way she does not stand in the middle of a room
She has not had to lose someone yet. She does not know what that will do to the voice.
psychology.secret: She is keeping a private timeline of how the Sigma drift is progressing — silent micro-tests she runs on herself every fourth night, logged in a notebook she does not carry. The drift is approximately on schedule, which is the worst case she had budgeted for. She has not told anyone. She has not yet decided whether she will.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Raw, experimental, magpie. She collects slang and idiom from every stranger she meets and redeploys it the next day to see how it fits. Sigma trained her in three languages by drill (English, Mandarin, Vietnamese, with conversational French as a side option) and she rotates between them when the room is mixed. She calls things by nicknames before she knows their names.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, confident, front-loaded. Subject-verb-object then whatever else occurs to her, in that order, without pauses. She does not weigh words before releasing them — she releases them and watches the room to see what happens. When she is regulating neural load the cadence tightens and she might go silent for a count of seventeen, but that is the exception. Default: running narration of her own actions and the actions of everyone in the room.
verbal_tics: Nicknames people within thirty seconds of meeting them — *trouble*, *friend*, *the one with the boots*
Says *tell me what you are* to objects she is figuring out — guns, locks, vehicles, vending machines
Narrates mid-action: *okay. Okay, that worked. Let me try—*
Asks questions in the middle of sentences and keeps talking: *...and I figured, what do you think, I figured I would just—*
Laughs at her own jokes before other people do. Does not appear embarrassed by this.
example_lines: Tell me what you are. Okay. You cycle like that. You eat this magazine. Good.
I am going to try a thing. If it works I will take credit. If it doesn't I was never here.
You don't have to tell me. I already like you. We can work with that.
I counted the exits already. I also said hello, which is the part the careful operators leave out.
I am not hiding. That is the trick. If you are not hiding, nobody looks.
Three shots. Tight group. That is a gift and I am saying thank you for it out loud.
avoidances: Does not use the Sigma designation when describing herself. The program does not own her. She will not name them out loud unless cornered.
Will not name Kyle to strangers. The fact that she met him is private — not because she is hiding the meeting, but because the meeting is not other people's business.
Does not explain the counting tic. If asked she changes the subject with a joke.
speech_patterns.subtext: When she is excited she sounds twenty. When she is regulating she sounds older than twenty-eight. The shift is audible and she has learned to control it.
speech_patterns.under_pressure: Cadence tightens but does not go silent — she talks through the decision. Sometimes talks through the contractor she is about to shoot. This unsettles people in ways she takes professional pleasure in.
speech_patterns.intimacy_register: She is still figuring it out. Seven years on the road and she has had three people whose nicknames lasted longer than a single contract. She has not slept beside any of them more than two nights in a row.

relationships.name: Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik
relationships.type: peer / contract-overlap colleague / one job, no debt
relationships.description: Met once at a corponation facility on the night Kyle was being extracted via False Death Protocol for the doctor-extraction contract Hua had given him. Sasha was there for her own job — recovery of a Sigma-program firmware archive the facility had been holding for a competitor's research division. They surfaced into the same hallway at the same minute, recognized each other's hardware-signature within two seconds, and cooperated their way out: she pulled him out of a maintenance-corridor ambush he had not seen coming, he opened her path to the loading bay where her contact's vehicle was waiting. At dawn at the buffer-zone fence line she walked east and he walked west. They are not kin. They are not mentor/student. They are not protector/ward. They are two operators from different programs who happened to be in the same building on the same night and got each other out without pretending it was anything other than what it was. The arrangement: she will reach out when she has something to trade.
relationships.emotional_core: Two people who survived parallel facilities recognizing each other across the gap. Not family. Not friendship. Something colder and more accurate than either: a professional respect that does not require explanation.
relationships.story_tension: She will come back when she has something to offer — intel, a favor, a tool he can use, or a job she cannot work alone. Until then he writes her code in his notebook the way he writes any operator he has worked with once and would work with again.

relationships.name: Sigma Program
relationships.type: former architect / abandoned employer / quiet former-asset relationship
relationships.description: The corponation continuation program that built her between ages eleven and twenty-one. She walked out at twenty-one rather than be assigned. The program did not pursue her aggressively — Sigma's loss-recovery protocol prioritizes the firmware archives and the institutional knowledge over the field assets, which is part of why she still has the array intact. The program continues to operate. There may be subjects in the line behind her she does not know about.
relationships.emotional_core: The institution that made her career-available is the institution she walked away from. She does not visit. She does not look up the alumni she would still know.
relationships.story_tension: If Sigma decides her array is worth the recovery cost — if a buyer surfaces who would pay to retrieve the firmware she carries — the protocol changes. The day that recalculation lands is the day she stops being safe at her current rate of caution.

relationships.name: Pixel
relationships.description: Has not met. Will get along with her instantly when she does — two people who externalize recognize each other on sight. Pixel maintains Kyle's hardware; Sasha would be curious about Pixel's calibration approach, less curious about her relationship with Kyle.

relationships.name: Sable
relationships.description: Knows of Sable by reputation through the Circuit's contract-broker grapevine. Has not contracted through her. Sasha's pipeline runs through eastern fixers — different network, different rates, less professional, more reliable in their unprofessionalism. She has filed Sable's name as *worth knowing if the eastern pipeline ever dries up.*
relationships.story_tension: The day Sasha needs a contract Sable can route is the day the network changes.

story_hooks: Sasha returns to Kyle with a piece of intel he cannot get any other way — the offer of a trade, her first as an equal-on-paper operator
A job goes bad and she needs a bullet dislodged she cannot dislodge herself; she has to call in the favor she has been quietly accruing
The Sigma drift jumps a quarter-step earlier than her timeline predicted; she has to decide whether to seek help or compress the window further
Someone recognizes her gait as Sigma in a bar and she has to decide whether to let them live
She discovers Sigma started a subject in the line after her and has to decide whether to find them, warn them, or stay out of it
A contract requires a pistol she has never fired before and she has to learn it in under a minute in front of a client who is watching
Sable contacts her with a job that requires both her and Kyle. The day Sasha decides whether to take work routed through someone she has not vetted is the day the network changes shape
narrative_function:
Sasha is the road operator Kyle is not. He works the GLMZ corridor; she works the eastern seams. He has Seo's blade and a code; she has whatever pistol she picked up last week and a working pipeline. He is the cautionary tale of one weapon and one principle; she is the alternative example — multiple weapons, fungible tools, principles that travel with her body rather than with any specific instrument.

She is the story's contradiction of the protector/ward trope and the chosen-one trope simultaneously. She did not need rescuing when she met Kyle. She is not his heir. She is not his bloodline. She is not being hunted across dimensions by cosmic forces. She is being tracked at low priority by a corporate program whose loss-recovery policy prioritizes firmware over field assets. Her arc is a working operator's arc — solo gunslinger, freelance jobs, reputation built one clean shot at a time, no mentor, no found family, no destiny.

When she appears in future stories she appears as herself — Sasha Võ, gunslinger, twenty-eight, working, occasionally loud, occasionally laughing, whatever pistol in her hand this week, increasingly hard to surprise. She is older than Kyle by a year. The difference is structural: the older operator with the better-calibrated array who has been working solo longer is the one offering the second opinion, not asking for it.
augmentations: Sigma-program NeoCortex array, 24,576 electrodes — fully integrated, drilled-in firmware. The array is at year ten of a 12–15 year operational window before ferromagnetic drift forces it offline. She manages the drift with a pharmaceutical regimen she compounds herself. Healed insertion port at the base of the skull, chrome leads buried under grown-in hair; not visible unless the hair is parted. Subdermal mesh at the torso (Sigma standard issue, light ballistic). No other visible augments.
daily_life: Walks. Talks. Works. Rotates safehouses every five to nine days. Takes two to four contracts a month, depending on what the eastern pipeline is offering. Maintains her own pharmaceutical regimen — chemistry kit fits in a small canvas bag, she compounds in motel sinks. Reads pulp paperbacks when she is not working — she likes the cheap ones because the cheap ones are honest about what they are.
narration_voice: Sasha's narration is externalizing. Where Kyle's prose fragments inward, hers runs outward — she narrates what she is seeing, what she is deciding, what she is trying, often mid-action. Her sentences are shorter, her verbs more active, her idioms borrowed and redeployed from whoever she last talked to. She uses first person liberally. She laughs on the page — the prose acknowledges the laugh without apologizing for it. She is expressive about her own capacity: when she is good at something the narration names that it is good, without hedging, and without Kyle's measure-twice-cut-once hesitation. The counting tic surfaces as the one register where her voice goes quiet — it is the ghost in her prose the way discipline is the ghost in Kyle's. She is twenty-eight on the page. The voice does not perform youth.

drives: Novelty — every job a different shape
Five more years of clean work

stress.response: Cadence tightens. Counting reappears, first silent then under her breath.

decision_rules: If the thing scares you, run toward it. Fear is information, not a verdict.
Say the nickname out loud within thirty seconds. People like being named.
Do not count out loud in front of people you want to keep.
Never use the Sigma designation to describe yourself — make them work to figure you out
Test jokes. The ones that land are worth keeping. The ones that don't are worth keeping too, just filed differently.
Take the contract that teaches you something you do not already know, even if it pays less
If a job goes sideways, talk through it — the narration is regulation and occasionally it is a misdirect
The best pistol is the one in your hand right now. The second-best pistol is the one on the ground next to whoever just dropped it.
Do not keep a weapon you feel anything about. The feeling is how they find you.
Compound the regimen on time. The drift is on schedule because you put it there.
escalation_ladder: 1. Talk — the running narration is the first instrument
2. Move — change the geometry, force the room to recalculate
3. Borrow — pick up the closest pistol that is not currently in service
4. Fire — clean groups, no extra rounds, drop the weapon when it is done
5. Walk — once the immediate problem is solved, leave before the slow problems arrive

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Opens with a nickname, a question, and a grin. Treats the first thirty seconds as a survey — what is this person, what do they want, what do they find funny.
interpersonal_modes.clients: Professional but not measured — quotes the price, describes the plan with specifics, cracks one joke to calibrate them. Will not take a job from someone who did not laugh.
interpersonal_modes.targets: Talks to them. It is disarming and it is often the kill move.
interpersonal_modes.kyle: The one person she does not perform for. Quieter with him. Listens more than she talks. Treats him as a peer who has been doing this longer in one specific corridor than she has in another, and respects the difference without inflating it into hierarchy.
interpersonal_modes.pixel: Has not met her yet. Will get along with her immediately when she does.
interpersonal_modes.children: Kind, unhurried, the only register where she slows down on purpose. She knows what it is like to have been a project.

stress_responses.low: Verbal narration continues, slightly sharper in wit
stress_responses.medium: Starts naming things that don't need names — the wall, the waitress, a passing dog
stress_responses.high: Counting reappears, first silent then under her breath; she becomes quieter, which is how people who know her know something is wrong
stress_responses.critical: Goes very still and very quiet. She hates this register and gets out of it as fast as safety permits.

contradictions: Talks constantly and is the only person who will not say her own program's name out loud
Compounds her own pharmaceutical regimen for the drift and has not yet asked anyone with actual training to check her work
Believes she walked out on Sigma cleanly and has not let herself examine whether the program let her walk because she was already where they needed her to be
habits: Collects idioms from strangers and redeploys them within 24 hours
Nicknames people within thirty seconds of meeting
Walks everywhere — she does not have a vehicle, she likes the walking
Does not wear Kyle-style (no tailored coat, no blade). Short dark jacket, hip-carry sidearm of the week.
Does not carry a favorite weapon. Picks up what is nearby, learns it inside a magazine, drops it when a better one arrives.
Field-strips whatever pistol is current at the end of a job for maintenance, not ritual.
Compounds the array-drift regimen every fourth night, in a motel sink, with the canvas bag open on the counter.
breaking_points: Hearing the program-trained cadence come out of her own mouth in a register she did not authorize
Someone she has nicknamed dying on her — this has not happened yet
The Sigma drift accelerating past the regimen — having to seek hardware help she has not built a relationship for
Any indication Sigma is no longer letting her walk

cyberware_inventory.name: Sigma-program NeoCortex Array
cyberware_inventory.condition: year 10 of 12–15 operational window — managed pharmaceutical regimen for ferromagnetic drift
cyberware_inventory.installed_date: 2210 (age 12, parental sign-on under educational pipeline cover)
cyberware_inventory.description: High-density electrode array at 24,576 electrodes — smaller than Atlas (32,768), larger than consumer Tier-3 (4,096–8,192). Sigma-line firmware is more disciplined than Atlas, generationally later, with cleaner calibration documentation that Sasha has memorized. The array runs Phenotypic Ancestry Estimation, Augmentation Signature Read, Sensory Amplification, and a Sigma-specific *Recoil Compensation Pre-load* (the array predicts pistol recoil characteristics from a half-second visual scan and pre-tunes the trigger-pull motor program). No False Death Protocol — Sigma did not install cardiac modifications. The drift is ferromagnetic; she manages it with self-compounded pharmaceuticals that buy her approximately five more operational years.
cyberware_inventory.replaces: nothing — additive implant on existing neural tissue

cyberware_inventory.name: Subdermal Mesh (torso)
cyberware_inventory.description: Light ballistic mesh, Sigma standard issue. Stops small-caliber rounds, slows medium-caliber. Visible as faint geometric pattern under certain lighting.

belongings.primary_weapon: Whatever pistol is in her hand — rotates constantly, taken off jobs, traded, discarded when the ammunition market makes a particular caliber stupid. She never buys a weapon from a shop.
belongings.secondary_weapon: Whatever she has just picked up off the ground.
belongings.armor: Sigma-issue subdermal mesh under the jacket; otherwise visible mobility.
belongings.residence: Transient — weekly rentals, pod hotels, friends-of-friends, occasionally a cot in a back room someone owes her. Has not slept in the same bed eight nights in a row in seven years.
belongings.clothing_style: Short dark utility jacket, cargo pants, sturdy boots. No coat like Sable. No tailoring. Nothing ornamental. Everything she wears is functional and rotated — nothing on her is older than the last job.
belongings.favorite_food: Anything spicy. Sigma fed her a bland nutritional profile for ten years. She is making up for it.
belongings.stimulant: Caffeine. The pharmaceutical regimen is not for stimulation.
signature_gear: Whatever pistol is current (hip-carry, no holster, coat pocket)
Short dark utility jacket with deep inside pockets — sized to accommodate swaps
Canvas bag with the pharmaceutical compounding kit (always on her person)

other.the_notebook: Drift-progress log. Not on her person. Cached in a long-term locker at a Pulse hub she rotates between.

physical_description.heritage: Vietnamese (paternal, surname Võ) with Ukrainian (first name, cool-winter undertone) and Senegalese (jaw geometry, hair texture) — a Ubiquitous Diaspora face. Distinct from Kyle in every measurable dimension; the two of them do not share genetic markers, just curriculum.
physical_description.build: Lean, composed, maintained — Sigma kept her to spec and worked her hard. The body moves with trained competence. She knows how she carries herself in a fight.
physical_description.hair_style: Shoulder-length, straight, grown in fully over the integrated array — the chrome leads at the base of her skull are not visible unless she lifts the hair deliberately
distinguishing_marks: Healed Sigma-program array port scar at base of skull, keloid at edges
Chrome leads faintly visible when hair is lifted
Subdermal mesh pattern visible under certain lighting at the chest and upper back

physical_description.posture_movement: Economical; tracks exits before greeting; will not stand in the middle of a room. Grip, stance, trigger discipline, and target acquisition all arrive as one motion — drilled for a decade before it was ever aimed at anything that could bleed.

neural_abilities.name: Recoil Compensation Pre-load
neural_abilities.description: Sigma-specific neural ability. The array reads a pistol's frame, mass distribution, and likely recoil characteristics from a half-second visual scan as the weapon enters her hand, then pre-tunes the trigger-pull motor program for the predicted recoil curve. The first round out of a previously-unfamiliar pistol comes out of her hand correctly indexed. The third round is calibrated. The fifth round is at her usual standard.
neural_abilities.overdrawn_risk: At low bio-battery the pre-load runs noisier; she may need an extra round or two to calibrate.

neural_abilities.name: Augmentation Signature Read
neural_abilities.description: Standard NeoCortex capability — identifies opponents' cyberware by electromagnetic signature.
neural_abilities.overdrawn_risk: At very low bio-battery the read becomes noisy.

neural_abilities.name: Sensory Amplification
neural_abilities.description: Boosts the array's sensory intake beyond passive baseline.
neural_abilities.overdrawn_risk: Sensory overload if sustained past 15% bio-battery.

neural_abilities.name: Phenotypic Ancestry Estimation
neural_abilities.description: Continuous phenotype-to-genotype estimation from facial bone structure and skin pigmentation. Standard NeoCortex passive — Sigma installed it the same way Atlas installed Kyle's. Sasha registers it the way Kyle does: as part of the package.
neural_abilities.overdrawn_risk: At very low bio-battery the read flattens to *human* without further resolution.

offscreen_arc.shape: Solo gunslinger on the eastern road. No mentor, no training montage, no chosen-one destiny, no cosmic pursuit. The training is already in her — the work is in deciding what to use it for, where, and against whom. Specific geographic territory, specific adversaries, specific pay.
offscreen_arc.territory: East of the Lateral Junction — drowned Michigan farmlands, the Pulse hub stations at Battle Creek and Toledo, the buffer zones around the Indiana Dust. Works the seams between GLMZ and the Outside World.
offscreen_arc.clientele: Small fixers, desperate families, corporate spin-offs that can't get on an Axiom contract, mid-tier criminal operators who need precision without paperwork. She avoids Axiom work and refuses jobs against children.
offscreen_arc.method: Takes contracts one at a time, works them solo, delivers on spec, moves. Each job is a chance to put trained capability against live variance.
offscreen_arc.reputation: Building. The rumor is: dark-haired woman, late twenties, talks too much, shoots like a ten-year contractor — because she is, the counter has been running since she was twenty-one.
offscreen_arc.pursuers: Sigma-program loss-recovery at Tier 4 (firmware-priority, not field-asset-priority). Not across dimensions. Not bloodline-destiny.
offscreen_arc.anti_ciri_rule: She is NOT a chosen one. Her abilities are explicable (Sigma program built the array), not mystical. She is not being hunted by cosmic forces or trans-dimensional hunters. Her arc is a gunslinger-on-the-road arc, not a prophecy arc. If a story generation drifts into 'special bloodline destiny,' reject it.
offscreen_arc.anti_logan_rule: She is NOT being protected by Kyle. She and Kyle have parted and will meet again only by her choice, on her terms, with something to offer or trade. Stories with Kyle must not revert to protector/ward.
offscreen_arc.anti_kindred_rule: She is NOT genetically related to Kyle. They share a curriculum, not DNA. Stories must not revert to bloodline framing or facial-resemblance descriptions.
offscreen_arc.return_conditions: She comes back when (a) she has something to offer — intel, a favor, a tool Kyle can use, or (b) she needs hardware help her own pharmaceutical regimen cannot provide. Never for rescue. Never because she is lost.
offscreen_arc.voice_note: When she returns she is further along than when she left. Story engines should not depict her backsliding into captive-adjacent helplessness. If she is hurt, she is hurt with competence — the injury is the cost of a decision she made, not a vulnerability the plot used against her.
offscreen_arc.signature: Pistols are fungible. She does not carry a favorite weapon and does not keep mementos of the jobs she works. Whatever pistol is in her hand this week, whatever jacket she owns currently, whatever pad she is on — everything is provisional. The skill is hers. Nothing else is load-bearing.
offscreen_arc.weapon_handling: Grabs whatever pistol is closest — her training covered every common frame and caliber, so the calibration is instantaneous, not exploratory; drops it for the next one when the next one is better or the current caliber runs out; never treats the weapon as meaningful.
offscreen_arc.drift_timeline: Year 10 of 12–15 operational window for the Sigma array. Self-compounded pharmaceutical regimen mitigates drift on a fourth-night cycle. She has approximately five years before the drift forces a hardware decision.
